alarm.opening: I want to make a alarm clock for my classes that is not distracting.
alarm.persona: A first-year college student who took one intro Python course.
facts: Wants it to run on a MacBook, not a phone.
Has written small Python scripts but never an app.
"Not distracting" means one quiet notification five minutes before class, nothing else.
Classes differ by day: Monday/Wednesday/Friday at 9:00, Tuesday/Thursday at 11:00.
Wants it working by next week.

club.opening: My club needs a website where members can sign up for events.
club.persona: A sophomore who is club treasurer and has built a static HTML page once.
facts: About 40 members; events have a capacity limit.
Sign-ups would collect names and student emails.
Club officers change every year, and someone else will have to run it.
Has never deployed anything to the internet.

grades.opening: I had an AI write me an app that tracks my grades but now it is broken and I do not know why.
grades.persona: A non-CS major who has been using an AI assistant to write all of the code.
facts: It is a Python script of about 300 lines that they did not write themselves.
It broke after they asked the AI to "add weighted categories."
There are no tests; they check it by running it and looking at the numbers.

plant.opening: I want my Raspberry Pi to text me when my plant needs water.
plant.persona: A hobbyist who has followed a few Raspberry Pi tutorials.
facts: Already has a soil-moisture sensor wired up and can print readings.
The readings sometimes jump to nonsense values for a moment.
The Wi-Fi in the apartment drops out at night.
Would be upset to get ten texts in a row, or none when the plant is dying.
